text: Etiology [Gr. aitia , cause, + logoV , discourse]: Ger. Ätiologie ; Fr. étiologie ; Ital. etiologia . (1) In philosophy: the science of CAUSE AND EFFECT (q.v.). (2) In medicine: the science of the causes of organic and mental disease. ( E.M. ) In biology: that branch of biology which deals with the origin and mode of development of organic beings. Introduced by Huxley ( Anatomy of Invertebrate Animals , Introd. 35, 1877), but not in general use. ( C.LL.M. - J.M.B. )
